headline: OpenAI reports improved jailbreak robustness after adversarial-data RL training
summary: A Nov 12 OpenAI paper describes an automated red-teaming loop that uses iterative attacker feedback and a repeated-success “worst@n” criterion to create adversarial training examples. In a controlled comparison, OpenAI reports that adding these examples to RL post-training raised safety scores from 45% to 68% on held-out fixed jailbreaks and from 71% to 92% on adaptive online attacks. The runs started from the same internal GPT-5.6-Terra checkpoint and used a fixed total RL budget. OpenAI also says it incorporated the approach into GPT-6 Astra and Sol training. These are first-party results, not independent confirmation; the paper discusses safety-judge bias and reports a cybersecurity benign-task utility decrease.
